title: Import transactions
description: Bring in a CSV or Excel export from your bank, check the rows, then add them to an account.

guide.title: What file can I import?
guide.intro: A CSV, XLSX or XLS export with a header row. Column names are matched in English, Greek or Dutch, ignoring case and accents.

date.label: Date
date.help: Date, Transaction date, Booking date, Ημερομηνία, Ημ/νία κίνησης…

amount.label: Amount
amount.help: Amount, Value, Ποσό. Negative is money out, positive is money in.

debitCredit.label: …or Debit and Credit
debitCredit.help: Two columns instead of Amount: Debit / Χρέωση is money out, Credit / Πίστωση is money in.

notes.header: Lines above the header row, like the bank name or account number, are skipped automatically.
notes.dates: Dates are read exactly in the format you pick below, never guessed. The template uses year first (2026-01-05).
notes.amounts: Both 1.234,56 and 1,234.56 work. Currency symbols are ignored.
notes.linked: Accounts connected through bank sync can't receive imports, because the bank already provides their transactions.

dateFormat.legend: How are dates written in your file?
dateFormat.help: Pick this before choosing the file. Dates that don't match are listed as skipped, never guessed.

upload.types: CSV, XLSX or XLS, up to 10 MB
upload.failed: The file could not be read.

review.noAccounts: You need an account that isn't connected to bank sync. Create one on the Accounts page first.
review.invertHelp: Use this for credit-card exports that show purchases as positive amounts.
review.duplicatesNote_one: {{count}} row looks like a transaction already in this account, so it was unticked.
review.duplicatesNote_other: {{count}} rows look like transactions already in this account, so they were unticked.
review.confirmFailed: The import failed. Nothing was saved.
